correctness.rationale: The proof is complete for every \(1\le p<\infty\) and every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\). On each interval, the upper-gradient inequality gives a continuous representative. For \(\alpha\ge1\), Hölder's inequality (with a separate \(p=1\) estimate) proves that oscillations vanish; component masses \(m_n\) equal \(\log2\) at \(\alpha=1\) and grow for \(\alpha>1\), so finite \(X_\alpha\) norm forces \(\inf_{I_n}|u|\to0\). For \(\alpha<1\), the sum of the component masses is finite and alternating component constants have upper gradient zero but no continuous representative. The endpoint and all quantifiers are explicit.
